rows.subtopic: Chemical Properties of Acids and Bases
rows.stem: Select a pair of olfactory indicators from the following :
rows.solution:
Olfactory indicators change their smell in an acidic or a basic medium. Clove oil and vanilla essence are both olfactory indicators: the smell of vanilla, for example, cannot be detected in a basic solution. Litmus, turmeric and methyl orange are indicators that change colour, not smell.

This is option (A) Clove oil and vanilla essence.

rows.stem: The balanced chemical equation showing reaction between quicklime and water is :
rows.solution:
Quicklime (calcium oxide) reacts vigorously with water to form slaked lime (calcium hydroxide), giving out a large amount of heat. No hydrogen or oxygen is formed:

\(\mathrm{CaO(s) + H_2O(l) \rightarrow Ca(OH)_2(aq)}\) + Heat

Check: Ca 1 = 1; O 2 = 2; H 2 = 2.

This is option (C) \(\mathrm{CaO + H_2O \longrightarrow Ca(OH)_2}\) + Heat.

rows.stem:
Study the following chemical reaction :

\(\mathrm{2\,Na\,(s) + 2\,H_2O\,(\mathit{l}) \longrightarrow 2\,NaOH\,(aq) + H_2\,(g)\uparrow}\)

The reducing agent in this reaction is :
rows.solution:
Sodium loses electrons and becomes \(\mathrm{Na^+}\) in NaOH, so it is oxidised. In doing so it reduces water: the hydrogen of water is set free as \(\mathrm{H_2}\). The substance that is oxidised and brings about reduction is the reducing agent.

This is option (A) Na.

rows.subtopic: Common Salt and Chemicals from It
rows.stem: Fresh milk has a pH of 6. To delay its curdling, a chemical substance is added to it, which is :
rows.solution:
A small amount of baking soda makes fresh milk slightly alkaline. The lactic acid formed as milk sours must first neutralise it, so the milk takes longer to set as curd. (Caustic soda and sodium carbonate are too strongly basic to add to food.)

This is option (D) Baking soda (Sodium hydrogen carbonate).

rows.stem: Which of the following statements is true for an amphoteric oxide ?

options.label: A
options.text: It reacts only with acid and does not form water.

options.label: B
options.text: It reacts with acid as well as base to form salt and hydrogen gas.

options.label: C
options.text: It reacts with both acid as well as base to form salt and water.

options.label: D
options.text: It reacts only with base and does not form water.

rows.solution:
An amphoteric oxide, such as aluminium oxide or zinc oxide, shows both acidic and basic behaviour: it reacts with acids and with bases, and in each case a salt and water are formed.

\(\mathrm{Al_2O_3 + 6HCl \rightarrow 2AlCl_3 + 3H_2O}\)

\(\mathrm{Al_2O_3 + 2NaOH \rightarrow 2NaAlO_2 + H_2O}\)

This is option (C) It reacts with both acid as well as base to form salt and water.

rows.subtopic: Chemical Properties of Acids and Bases
rows.stem: Hydronium ions are formed by the reaction between :
rows.solution:
Hydrogen chloride gas dissolves in water to give hydrogen ions, which cannot exist alone and combine with water molecules to form hydronium ions:

\(\mathrm{HCl + H_2O \rightarrow H_3O^+ + Cl^-}\)

Sodium hydroxide gives hydroxide ions, while calcium chloride and ethanol give no hydrogen ions.

This is option (C) Hydrogen chloride gas and water.

rows.stem: The correct representation of covalent bonding in an oxygen molecule is :

options.label: A
options.text: Diagram (A) as printed - an electron-dot diagram of two overlapping atoms; see the attached figure.

options.label: B
options.text: Diagram (B) as printed - an electron-dot diagram of two overlapping atoms; see the attached figure.

options.label: C
options.text: Diagram (C) as printed - an electron-dot diagram of two overlapping atoms; see the attached figure.

options.label: D
options.text: Diagram (D) as printed - an electron-dot diagram of two overlapping atoms; see the attached figure.

rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - all four options are drawn electron-dot (cross and dot) diagrams of two overlapping circles, each atom's electrons shown as crosses on one side and dots on the other; the options ARE the figure, and how many electrons each diagram places in the shared region is exactly what is tested, so the placeholders below withhold it. Page idx 4.
rows.solution:
An oxygen atom (2, 6) has six valence electrons and needs two more. Two oxygen atoms therefore share two pairs of electrons, forming a double bond, and each atom then has eight electrons around it.

So the correct diagram shows four electrons in the shared region (two crosses and two dots), with each atom keeping four more electrons of its own (six valence electrons in all). The diagram with exactly this arrangement is the first one. The diagrams with a single shared pair, or with three shared pairs, do not give each oxygen atom six valence electrons and an octet.

This is option (A).

rows.stem: The process in which loss of water in the form of vapours from the aerial parts of plants takes place is *X*, which helps in *Y*. Here *X* and *Y* respectively are :

options.label: C
options.text: translocation and movement of soluble products of photosynthesis in phloem.

options.label: D
options.text: translocation and absorption of water and minerals from soil by roots.

rows.solution:
The loss of water as vapour from the aerial parts of a plant, mainly through the stomata of the leaves, is transpiration (X). Transpiration helps in the absorption and upward movement of water and minerals, and in temperature regulation (Y). Translocation is the transport of the soluble products of photosynthesis, which is a different process.

This is option (B) transpiration and temperature regulation.

rows.stem: As compared to terrestrial organisms, the rate of breathing in aquatic organisms is :

options.label: A
options.text: faster because they need more oxygen for their survival.

options.label: B
options.text: faster because the amount of dissolved oxygen in water is fairly low.

options.label: C
options.text: slower because the amount of dissolved oxygen in water is fairly low.

options.label: D
options.text: slower because the capacity of water of dissolving atmospheric air is limited.

rows.solution:
The amount of oxygen dissolved in water is fairly low compared with the amount of oxygen in the air. So aquatic organisms have to breathe much faster than terrestrial organisms to get enough oxygen.

This is option (B) faster because the amount of dissolved oxygen in water is fairly low.

rows.stem:
Consider the following two statements :

(i) The trait that expresses itself in \(\mathrm{F_1}\) generation.

(ii) The trait that keeps on passing from one generation to another.

The appropriate terms for the statements (i) and (ii) respectively are :
rows.solution:
(i) The trait that expresses itself in the \(\mathrm{F_1}\) generation is the dominant trait.

(ii) A trait that keeps passing from one generation to the next is an inherited trait.

This is option (C) Dominant trait, Inherited trait.

rows.stem: The part in which gustatory receptors are present in our body is :
rows.solution:
Gustatory receptors detect taste, and they are present on the tongue. (The inner lining of the nose has the olfactory receptors, for smell.)

This is option (C) tongue.

rows.stem: The bacterial and the viral infections that may be caused due to unsafe sex respectively are :
rows.solution:
Syphilis is a sexually transmitted disease caused by bacteria, and warts are caused by a virus. (Gonorrhoea is also bacterial, while HIV-AIDS is viral.)

This is option (D) Syphilis and Warts.

rows.stem: The expressions that relate (i) Q, I and t and (ii) Q, V and W respectively are (Here the symbols have their usual meanings) :
rows.solution:
(i) Current is the charge flowing per unit time, \(I = \dfrac{Q}{t}\), so \(Q = I \times t\).

(ii) Potential difference is the work done per unit charge, \(V = \dfrac{W}{Q}\), so \(W = V \times Q\).

This is option (B) (i) \(\mathrm{Q = I \times t}\) (ii) \(\mathrm{W = V \times Q}\).

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Current-carrying Conductor
rows.stem: A constant current flows in a horizontal wire in the plane of the paper from east to west as shown in the figure. The direction of the magnetic field will be north to south at a point :

options.label: C
options.text: located in the plane of the paper on the north side of the wire.

options.label: D
options.text: located in the plane of the paper on the south side of the wire.

rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - a compass cross labelled N, S, E and W above a horizontal wire drawn with an arrow from E towards W; the stem already states the current flows east to west in the plane of the paper, so the row is answerable from text. Page idx 8.
rows.solution:
By the right-hand thumb rule, point the thumb along the current, from east to west. The fingers then curl round the wire so that below the wire the field points from north to south, and above the wire it points from south to north.

This is option (B) directly below the wire.

rows.stem: An electric kettle consumes 1 kW of electric power when operated at 220 V. The minimum rating of the fuse wire to be used for it is
rows.solution:
The current drawn by the kettle is

\(I = \dfrac{P}{V} = \dfrac{1000}{220} \approx 4{\cdot}55\) A.

The fuse must allow at least this current, so the lowest rating that works is 5 A. (A 4 A fuse would melt during normal use.)

This is option (D) 5 A.

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Solenoid
rows.stem: For a current in a long straight solenoid, N and S poles are created at the two ends. Among the following statements, the *incorrect* statement is :

options.label: A
options.text: The magnetic field lines inside the solenoid are in the form of straight lines, which indicates that the magnetic field is uniform at all points inside the solenoid.

options.label: B
options.text: The strong magnetic field produced inside the solenoid can magnetize the soft iron placed inside it.

options.label: C
options.text: The pattern of the magnetic field associated with a current carrying solenoid is different from the pattern of the magnetic field around a bar magnet.

options.label: D
options.text: The N and S poles exchange positions when the direction of current through the solenoid is reversed.

rows.solution:
The magnetic field pattern of a current-carrying solenoid is similar to that of a bar magnet: one end behaves as a north pole and the other as a south pole. So the statement that the two patterns are different is incorrect. The other three statements are true.

The incorrect statement is option (C) The pattern of the magnetic field associated with a current carrying solenoid is different from the pattern of the magnetic field around a bar magnet.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** In the following reaction

\(\mathrm{ZnO + C \longrightarrow Zn + CO}\)

ZnO undergoes reduction.

**Reason (R) :** Carbon is a reducing agent that reduces ZnO to Zn.
rows.context: For questions number 17 to 20, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (a), (b), (c) and (d) as given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
In the reaction, ZnO loses oxygen to become Zn, so ZnO is reduced and the Assertion is true. Carbon takes up the oxygen and is oxidised to CO; a substance that removes oxygen in this way is a reducing agent, so the Reason is true and explains why ZnO is reduced.

The Reason is true and explains the Assertion. This is option (A).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Human populations show a great deal of variations in traits.

**Reason (R) :** All variations in a species have equal chances of surviving in the environment in which they live.
rows.context: For questions number 17 to 20, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (a), (b), (c) and (d) as given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Human populations show a great deal of variation in traits, so the Assertion is true. But all variations do not have equal chances of surviving: depending on the nature of the variation, some individuals are better suited to the environment and survive, so the Reason is false.

The Assertion is true while the Reason is false, which is option (C).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** The walls of atria are thicker than those of the ventricles.

**Reason (R) :** Ventricles have to pump blood into various organs at high pressure.
rows.context: For questions number 17 to 20, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (a), (b), (c) and (d) as given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
The ventricles have to pump blood to the various organs at high pressure, so their walls are thicker than those of the atria. The Assertion is false and the Reason is true.

The Assertion is false while the Reason is true, which is option (D).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Two magnetic field lines around a current carrying straight wire do not intersect each other.

**Reason (R) :** The magnitude of the magnetic field produced at a given point increases as the current through the wire increases.
rows.context: For questions number 17 to 20, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (a), (b), (c) and (d) as given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Two magnetic field lines never intersect, because at the point of intersection the compass needle would have to point in two directions at once. The Assertion is true.

The field produced at a given point does increase as the current through the wire increases, so the Reason is also true. But it says nothing about why field lines cannot cross.

Both are true and the Reason is not the correct explanation, which is option (B).

rows.subtopic: Common Salt and Chemicals from It
rows.stem:
On heating ‘X’ at 373 K, it loses water molecules and becomes ‘Y’. ‘Y’ is a substance which doctors use for supporting fractured bones in the right position.

(i) Identify ‘X’ and ‘Y’.

(ii) How can ‘X’ be reobtained from ‘Y’ ?
rows.solution:
(i) X is gypsum, calcium sulphate dihydrate, \(\mathrm{CaSO_4 \cdot 2H_2O}\). On heating at 373 K it loses water and becomes Y, Plaster of Paris (calcium sulphate hemihydrate), \(\mathrm{CaSO_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}H_2O}\), which doctors use to support fractured bones.

\(\mathrm{CaSO_4 \cdot 2H_2O \xrightarrow{373\text{ K}} CaSO_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}H_2O + 1\frac{1}{2}H_2O}\)

(ii) X is obtained again by mixing Plaster of Paris with water; it sets as a hard solid mass of gypsum:

\(\mathrm{CaSO_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}H_2O + 1\frac{1}{2}H_2O \rightarrow CaSO_4 \cdot 2H_2O}\)

rows.stem:
Two solutions M and N give Red and Blue colour respectively with a universal indicator.

(i) In which solution will the hydrogen ion concentration be more ? Justify your answer.

(ii) If both M and N solutions are mixed and the resultant mixture is tested with a universal indicator, it turns green. What is the nature of the salt formed ? Justify your answer.
rows.solution:
(i) The hydrogen ion concentration is more in M. M gives a red colour with universal indicator, so it is an acidic solution (low pH), while N, which gives a blue colour, is basic.

(ii) The salt formed is neutral. M is an acid and N is a base; they neutralise each other, and the green colour with universal indicator shows a pH of 7.

rows.stem: Write the name and function of parts (i) and (ii) in the diagram of a neuron given below.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the parts to be named exist only as two pointers on a drawn neuron (cell body with branching processes, a long sheathed fibre and branched endings), labelled (i) and (ii); which structure each pointer marks is the answer and is withheld here. Page idx 12.
rows.solution:
(i) Dendrite (the branched endings of the cell body). The dendrites acquire information: they receive the stimulus and set off a chemical reaction that creates an electrical impulse.

(ii) Axon (the long fibre, covered by the sheath). The information travels along the axon as an electrical impulse, from the cell body to its end.

rows.stem: List the events in proper sequence that take place during the process of photosynthesis.
rows.solution:
The events of photosynthesis, in order:

(i) Absorption of light energy by chlorophyll.

(ii) Conversion of light energy to chemical energy, and splitting of water molecules into hydrogen and oxygen.

(iii) Reduction of carbon dioxide to carbohydrates.

rows.stem: Explain in brief two ways by which leaves of a plant help in excretion.
rows.solution:
Any two:

1. Plants get rid of excess water by transpiration, through the stomata of the leaves.

2. Oxygen, a by-product of photosynthesis, is given out through the stomata of the leaves.

3. Many waste products are stored in the leaves, and these are removed when the leaves fall off.

rows.stem: In the process of digestion of food in human beings, two protein-digesting enzymes are secreted. Name the enzymes along with the glands that secrete them.
rows.solution: Pepsin is secreted by the gastric glands in the wall of the stomach. Trypsin is secreted by the pancreas; it digests proteins in the small intestine.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.subtopic: Defects of Vision and their Correction
rows.stem:
Observe the following diagram showing an image formation in an eye :

(a) Identify the defect of vision shown in the figure.

(b) List its two causes and suggest a suitable corrective lens to overcome this defect.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the defect exists only in the drawing: rays from a point object on the axis pass through the eye lens of a drawn eyeball, with dashed extensions beyond the back of the eye; where the rays meet relative to the retina is the quantity under test and is withheld here. Page idx 14.
rows.solution:
(a) In the figure, the rays from a near object meet behind the retina, so the image is not formed on it. The defect is hypermetropia (far-sightedness).

(b) Causes: (i) the focal length of the eye lens is too long; (ii) the eyeball has become too small.

It is corrected by a convex (converging) lens of suitable power.

rows.stem:
In the following food chain, if 50 J of energy was available to the hawk, how much energy would have been present at the first and third tropic levels ? Justify your answer.

Grass \(\longrightarrow\) Grasshopper \(\longrightarrow\) Frog \(\longrightarrow\) Snake \(\longrightarrow\) Hawk
rows.solution:
Only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level reaches the next level (the 10 percent law). So, going back along the chain, the energy at each level is 10 times that at the level after it.

Hawk (fifth level) 50 J; snake 500 J; frog (third level) 5000 J; grasshopper 50,000 J; grass (first level) 500,000 J.

So the energy present at the first trophic level is 500,000 J (5,00,000 J) and at the third trophic level 5000 J.

rows.stem:
(a) Define a double displacement reaction.

(b) Write the chemical equation of a double displacement reaction which is also a (i) Neutralization reaction and (ii) Precipitation reaction. Give justification for your answer.
rows.solution:
(a) A double displacement reaction is a reaction in which there is an exchange of ions between the reactants.

(b) (i) \(\mathrm{HCl + NaOH \rightarrow NaCl + H_2O}\)

The acid and the base exchange ions and form a salt and water, so this is a neutralisation reaction.

(ii) \(\mathrm{Na_2SO_4(aq) + BaCl_2(aq) \rightarrow BaSO_4(s) + 2NaCl(aq)}\)

The ions are exchanged and an insoluble white substance, barium sulphate, is formed as a precipitate, so this is a precipitation reaction.

rows.subtopic: Common Salt and Chemicals from It
rows.stem:
(a) Sometimes the pH of our mouth gets lower than \(5{\cdot}5\). Why ?

(b) A basic salt ‘X’ is obtained by heating baking soda followed by crystallisation. Identify ‘X’ and state its two industrial uses.

(c) Why do copper sulphate crystals turn white on heating ?
rows.solution:
(a) Bacteria present in the mouth break down the sugar and food particles left in the mouth after eating and produce acids. These acids lower the pH of the mouth below \(5{\cdot}5\), and tooth decay then starts.

(b) X is washing soda, sodium carbonate decahydrate, \(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3 \cdot 10H_2O}\). Heating baking soda gives sodium carbonate, and recrystallising it from water gives washing soda.

Uses (any two): in the glass, soap and paper industries; in the manufacture of borax; as a cleaning agent; for removing permanent hardness of water.

(c) On heating, copper sulphate crystals lose their water of crystallisation, and the anhydrous salt is white:

\(\mathrm{CuSO_4 \cdot 5H_2O \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} CuSO_4 + 5H_2O}\)

rows.stem:
(a) With the help of an activity, explain the action of saliva on the food we eat.

(b) Why is bile juice important in the process of digestion ?
rows.solution:
(a) Activity: take 1 mL of 1% starch solution in each of two test tubes, A and B. Add 1 mL of saliva to test tube A, and leave both test tubes undisturbed for 20 to 30 minutes. Then add a few drops of dilute iodine solution to both.

Observation: the solution in test tube B turns blue-black, because it still contains starch. The colour does not change to blue-black in test tube A, because the enzyme in saliva (salivary amylase) has broken the starch down into sugar.

So saliva breaks down starch, a complex molecule, into simple sugar.

(b) Any one: bile makes the acidic food coming from the stomach alkaline, so that the pancreatic enzymes can act on it; bile salts emulsify fats, breaking large fat globules into smaller ones so that the enzymes can digest them more easily.

rows.subtopic: Lens Formula and Power of a Lens
rows.stem:
(i) An object of 5 cm height is placed at a distance of 20 cm from the optical centre of a concave lens of focal length 18 cm. Calculate (1) image distance and (2) the magnification in this case.

(ii) Compare the values of magnification obtained by a concave lens and a convex lens when both the lenses form virtual images.
rows.solution:
(i) Given \(h = 5\) cm, \(u = -20\) cm and \(f = -18\) cm (concave lens).

(1) By the lens formula \(\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}\),

\(\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{u} + \dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{-20} + \dfrac{1}{-18} = -\dfrac{18 + 20}{360} = -\dfrac{38}{360}\)

\(v = -\dfrac{360}{38} \approx -9{\cdot}47\) cm.

The image is \(9{\cdot}47\) cm from the lens on the same side as the object.

(2) \(m = \dfrac{v}{u} = \dfrac{-9{\cdot}47}{-20} \approx 0{\cdot}47\).

(ii) Both virtual images are erect, so both magnifications are positive. The virtual image formed by a convex lens is enlarged, so \(m > 1\); that formed by a concave lens is diminished, so \(m < 1\).

rows.stem: A convex lens can form a (i) real, inverted and magnified image as well as (ii) virtual, erect and magnified image of an object. If the focal length of the lens is 10 cm, what should be the range of the object distance in both cases ? Draw ray diagrams to justify your answer.
rows.solution:
For \(f = 10\) cm, F is at 10 cm and 2F at 20 cm from the lens.

(i) A real, inverted and magnified image is formed when the object is between F and 2F: the object distance is between 10 cm and 20 cm.

(ii) A virtual, erect and magnified image is formed when the object is between the optical centre and F: the object distance is less than 10 cm.

Ray diagram (i): place the object AB between F and 2F. A ray from A parallel to the principal axis passes, after refraction, through the focus on the other side; a ray from A through the optical centre goes straight on. They meet beyond 2F on the other side, below the axis: the image is real, inverted and magnified.

Ray diagram (ii): place the object between the optical centre and F. The ray parallel to the axis refracts through the focus on the other side, and the ray through the optical centre goes straight on. The two refracted rays diverge; produced backwards (dotted), they meet on the same side as the object, above the axis and farther from the lens: the image is virtual, erect and magnified.

Draw arrows on all the rays.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem:
(a) State one important function of the following parts of the human eye :

(i) Retina

(ii) Pupil

(b) State the role of ciliary muscles in focussing objects at varying distances from the eye.
rows.solution:
(a) (i) Retina: a light-sensitive screen on which the image of an object is formed.

(ii) Pupil: it regulates and controls the amount of light entering the eye.

(b) The ciliary muscles change the curvature of the eye lens, and so its focal length. When they relax, the lens becomes thin and its focal length increases, so distant objects are seen clearly. When they contract, the lens becomes thick and its focal length decreases, so nearby objects are seen clearly.

rows.stem:
(i) A straight cylindrical conductor is suspended with its axis perpendicular to the magnetic field of a horse-shoe magnet. The conductor gets displaced towards left when a current is passed through it. What will happen to the displacement of the conductor if the

(1) current through it is increased ?

(2) horse-shoe magnet is replaced by another stronger horse-shoe magnet ?

(3) direction of current through it is reversed ?

(ii) Name and state the rule for determining the direction of force on a current carrying conductor in a magnetic field.
rows.solution:
(i) (1) The displacement of the conductor increases.

(2) The displacement increases.

(3) The direction of displacement is reversed: the conductor is displaced towards the right.

(ii) Fleming's left-hand rule. Stretch the thumb, forefinger and middle finger of the left hand so that they are mutually perpendicular. If the forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field and the middle finger in the direction of the current, then the thumb points in the direction of motion of, or the force acting on, the conductor.

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Current-carrying Conductor
rows.stem: Draw the pattern of the magnetic field produced around a vertical current carrying straight conductor passing through a horizontal cardboard. Mark the direction of current and the magnetic field lines. Name and state the rule which is used to determine the direction of magnetic field associated with a current carrying conductor.
rows.solution:
Diagram: a straight conductor passes vertically through a horizontal cardboard and is connected to a battery and a plug key (a rheostat and an ammeter may be included). On the cardboard, draw concentric circles centred on the conductor, closer together near the wire. Mark the direction of the current along the wire with an arrow and the direction of the field lines with arrows on the circles: for a current flowing upward the field lines run anticlockwise when seen from above, and for a current flowing downward they run clockwise.

Rule: the right-hand thumb rule. Imagine holding the current-carrying straight conductor in the right hand so that the thumb points in the direction of the current. Then the fingers wrap around the conductor in the direction of the field lines of the magnetic field.

rows.stem: How is ozone formed in the higher levels of the atmosphere ? “Damage to the ozone layer is a cause of concern.” Justify this statement.
rows.solution:
At the higher levels of the atmosphere, ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the sun splits oxygen molecules into free oxygen atoms. These atoms combine with oxygen molecules to form ozone:

\(\mathrm{O_2 \xrightarrow{\text{UV}} O + O}\)

\(\mathrm{O + O_2 \rightarrow O_3}\)

The ozone layer shields the earth from the harmful UV radiation of the sun. If it is damaged, more UV radiation reaches the earth and causes harmful effects such as skin cancer in human beings, so its damage is a cause of concern.

rows.stem:
A neutral organic compound ‘X’ (Molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_2H_6O}\)) on reacting with acidified \(\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7}\) gives an organic compound ‘Y’ which is acidic in nature. ‘X’ reacts with ‘Y’ on warming in the presence of conc. \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) to give a sweet smelling compound ‘Z’.

(i) Identify ‘X’, ‘Y’ and ‘Z’.

(ii) Write the chemical equations for the reactions in the conversion of (1) ‘X’ to ‘Y’ and (2) ‘X’ to ‘Z’.

(iii) State the role of (1) acidified \(\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7}\) in the conversion of ‘X’ to ‘Y’ and (2) conc. \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) in the reaction of ‘X’ and ‘Y’.

(iv) Name the reaction which occurs when ‘Z’ reacts with an alkali.
rows.solution:
(i) X (\(\mathrm{C_2H_6O}\), neutral) is ethanol, \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH}\). Y (acidic) is ethanoic acid (acetic acid), \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\). Z (sweet smelling) is the ester ethyl ethanoate (ethyl acetate), \(\mathrm{CH_3COOC_2H_5}\).

(ii) (1) X to Y:

\(\mathrm{C_2H_5OH \xrightarrow{\text{acidified } K_2Cr_2O_7} CH_3COOH}\)

(2) X to Z:

\(\mathrm{CH_3COOH + C_2H_5OH \xrightarrow{\text{conc. } H_2SO_4,\ \text{heat}} CH_3COOC_2H_5 + H_2O}\)

(iii) (1) Acidified \(\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7}\) is an oxidising agent: it provides oxygen to oxidise ethanol to ethanoic acid.

(2) Conc. \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) is a dehydrating agent: it helps remove the water formed in the reaction.

(iv) Saponification. With an alkali such as sodium hydroxide, the ester is converted back to the alcohol and the sodium salt of the acid:

\(\mathrm{CH_3COOC_2H_5 + NaOH \rightarrow C_2H_5OH + CH_3COONa}\)

rows.stem:
Carry out the following conversions, stating the condition(s) for each :

(i) Ethanol \(\longrightarrow\) Ethene

(ii) Ethene \(\longrightarrow\) Ethane

(iii) Ethane \(\longrightarrow\) Chloroethane

(iv) Ethanol \(\longrightarrow\) Ethanoic acid

(v) Ethanoic acid \(\longrightarrow\) Ethyl ethanoate
rows.solution:
(i) Ethanol is heated at 443 K with excess concentrated sulphuric acid, which removes water from it:

\(\mathrm{C_2H_5OH \xrightarrow{\text{conc. } H_2SO_4,\ 443\text{ K}} C_2H_4 + H_2O}\)

(ii) Ethene adds hydrogen in the presence of a nickel or palladium catalyst:

\(\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH_2 + H_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Ni or Pd}} CH_3{-}CH_3}\)

(iii) Ethane reacts with chlorine in the presence of sunlight (substitution):

\(\mathrm{C_2H_6 + Cl_2 \xrightarrow{\text{sunlight}} C_2H_5Cl + HCl}\)

(iv) Ethanol is oxidised by heating with alkaline potassium permanganate or acidified potassium dichromate:

\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH \xrightarrow{\text{alkaline } KMnO_4 \text{ or acidified } K_2Cr_2O_7,\ \text{heat}} CH_3COOH}\)

(v) Ethanoic acid is warmed with ethanol in the presence of an acid catalyst (esterification):

\(\mathrm{CH_3COOH + C_2H_5OH \xrightarrow{\text{acid}} CH_3COOC_2H_5 + H_2O}\)

rows.stem:
(i) Where are testes located in the human males and why ? State two function of the testes.

(ii) In the human female, one of the ovaries releases an egg every month. State the changes that take place if

(1) the egg is fertilized, and

(2) the egg is not fertilized.

(iii) What is done during the surgical method in males and females to prevent pregnancy ?
rows.solution:
(i) The testes are located outside the abdominal cavity, in the scrotum, because the formation of sperms requires a temperature lower than the normal body temperature.

Functions: formation of sperms (the male gametes); production of the male sex hormone, testosterone.

(ii) (1) If the egg is fertilised, the fertilised egg (zygote) starts dividing to form an embryo, which gets implanted in the thick, blood-rich lining of the uterus.

(2) If the egg is not fertilised, the thick inner lining of the uterus is not needed. It slowly breaks and comes out through the vagina as blood and mucus (menstruation).

(iii) In males the vas deferens is blocked (vasectomy), so the sperms cannot pass. In females the fallopian tube is blocked (tubectomy), so the egg cannot reach the uterus.

rows.stem:
(i) What happens when :

(1) Leaves of Bryophyllum fall on the soil ?

(2) Planaria is cut into many pieces ?

(3) Sporangia of Rhizopus on maturation liberate spores ?

Mention the modes of reproduction in each of the above three cases.

(ii) Write the changes that occur in a flower once the fertilisation has taken place.
rows.solution:
(i) (1) Buds produced in the notches along the margins of Bryophyllum leaves begin to grow into new plants when the leaves fall on the soil. Mode: vegetative propagation.

(2) Each piece of Planaria grows into a complete organism. Mode: regeneration.

(3) The spores begin to grow into new Rhizopus individuals after reaching a suitable moist surface. Mode: spore formation.

(ii) After fertilisation:

1. The zygote divides several times to form an embryo within the ovule.

2. The ovule develops a tough coat and is gradually converted into a seed.

3. The ovary grows rapidly and ripens to form a fruit.

4. The petals, sepals, stamens, style and stigma may shrivel and fall off.

rows.stem:
(a) State Ohm’s Law.

(b) Name and define the physical quantity determined by the slope of V – I curve given in the diagram. Use this graph to find the value of this physical quantity in SI units.

(c) Establish the relationship between 1 kWh and 1 joule.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - part (b) reads its value off the printed graph: Potential Difference (V) on the vertical axis with ticks 0, 1·5, 3·0, 4·5, 6·0 and Current (A) on the horizontal axis with ticks 0, 0·2, 0·4, 0·6, 0·8, and a straight line from the origin; the point the line reaches is the data for the answer and is withheld here. Page idx 22.
rows.solution:
(a) Ohm's law: the potential difference V across the ends of a given metallic wire in an electric circuit is directly proportional to the current flowing through it, provided its temperature remains the same. That is, \(V \propto I\), or \(V = IR\).

(b) The slope of the V-I graph gives the resistance, R. Resistance is the property of a conductor to resist the flow of charges through it.

From the graph, \(V = 6{\cdot}0\) V when \(I = 0{\cdot}8\) A, so

\(R = \text{slope} = \dfrac{V}{I} = \dfrac{6{\cdot}0 - 0}{0{\cdot}8 - 0} = \dfrac{60}{8} = 7{\cdot}5\,\Omega\).

(c) 1 kWh is the energy used in one hour at a rate of 1000 W:

\(1\) kWh \(= 1000\) W \(\times 3600\) s \(= 3{\cdot}6 \times 10^6\) W s \(= 3{\cdot}6 \times 10^6\) J.

rows.stem: Name an ore of Mercury and state the form in which Mercury is present in it.
rows.context:
Metals are required for a variety of purposes. For this we need their extraction from their ores. Ores mined from the earth are usually contaminated with many impurities which must be removed prior to the extraction of metals. The extraction of pure metal involves the following steps :

(1) Concentration of ore

(2) Extraction of the metal from the concentrated ore

(3) Refining of the metal
rows.solution: Cinnabar is an ore of mercury. Mercury is present in it as its sulphide, HgS.

rows.stem: What happens to zinc carbonate when it is heated strongly in a limited supply of air ?
rows.context:
Metals are required for a variety of purposes. For this we need their extraction from their ores. Ores mined from the earth are usually contaminated with many impurities which must be removed prior to the extraction of metals. The extraction of pure metal involves the following steps :

(1) Concentration of ore

(2) Extraction of the metal from the concentrated ore

(3) Refining of the metal
rows.solution:
Zinc carbonate decomposes into zinc oxide and carbon dioxide. Heating an ore strongly in a limited supply of air is called calcination:

\(\mathrm{ZnCO_3(s) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} ZnO(s) + CO_2(g)}\)

rows.stem:
The reaction of a metal A with \(\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}\) is highly exothermic and is used to join railway tracks.

(I) Identify the metal A and name the reaction taking place.

(II) Write the chemical equation for the reaction of metal A with \(\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}\).
rows.context:
Metals are required for a variety of purposes. For this we need their extraction from their ores. Ores mined from the earth are usually contaminated with many impurities which must be removed prior to the extraction of metals. The extraction of pure metal involves the following steps :

(1) Concentration of ore

(2) Extraction of the metal from the concentrated ore

(3) Refining of the metal
rows.solution:
(I) Metal A is aluminium. The reaction is the thermit reaction.

(II) \(\mathrm{Fe_2O_3 + 2Al \rightarrow 2Fe + Al_2O_3}\) + Heat

The heat produced is so large that the iron formed is molten, which is why the reaction is used to join railway tracks.

rows.stem: We cannot use carbon to obtain sodium from sodium oxide. Why ? State the reactions taking place at cathode and anode during electrolytic reduction of sodium chloride.
rows.context:
Metals are required for a variety of purposes. For this we need their extraction from their ores. Ores mined from the earth are usually contaminated with many impurities which must be removed prior to the extraction of metals. The extraction of pure metal involves the following steps :

(1) Concentration of ore

(2) Extraction of the metal from the concentrated ore

(3) Refining of the metal
rows.solution:
Sodium is highly reactive and has more affinity for oxygen than carbon has, so carbon cannot remove oxygen from sodium oxide. Sodium is therefore obtained by the electrolytic reduction of molten sodium chloride.

At the cathode: \(\mathrm{Na^+ + e^- \rightarrow Na}\)

At the anode: \(\mathrm{2Cl^- \rightarrow Cl_2 + 2e^-}\)

rows.stem: State the basis on which the sex of a newborn baby is determined in humans.
rows.context: In some families, either rural or urban, females are tortured for giving birth to a female child. They do not seem to understand the scientific reason behind the birth of a boy or a girl. In fact the mother is not responsible for the sex of the child and it has been genetically proved that the sex of a newborn is determined by what the child inherits from the father.
rows.solution: A mother has a pair of X chromosomes, so every egg carries an X chromosome. A father has an X and a Y chromosome, so half his sperms carry X and half carry Y. If a sperm carrying X fertilises the egg, the child is a girl (XX); if a sperm carrying Y fertilises it, the child is a boy (XY). So the sex of the child depends on which chromosome it inherits from the father.

rows.stem: Why is the pair of sex chromosomes called a mismatched pair in males ?
rows.context: In some families, either rural or urban, females are tortured for giving birth to a female child. They do not seem to understand the scientific reason behind the birth of a boy or a girl. In fact the mother is not responsible for the sex of the child and it has been genetically proved that the sex of a newborn is determined by what the child inherits from the father.
rows.solution: In males the sex chromosomes are X and Y. The X is a normal-sized chromosome while the Y is a short one, so the two do not match, and the pair is called a mismatched pair.

rows.stem: How is the original number of chromosomes present in the parents restored in the progeny ?
rows.context: In some families, either rural or urban, females are tortured for giving birth to a female child. They do not seem to understand the scientific reason behind the birth of a boy or a girl. In fact the mother is not responsible for the sex of the child and it has been genetically proved that the sex of a newborn is determined by what the child inherits from the father.
rows.solution: During the formation of germ cells (gametes), the number of chromosomes is reduced to half, so each gamete has only one set. When two germ cells from the two parents combine at fertilisation to form the zygote, the original number of chromosomes is restored in the progeny.

rows.stem: Explain by giving two examples of the organisms in which the sex is not genetically determined.
rows.context: In some families, either rural or urban, females are tortured for giving birth to a female child. They do not seem to understand the scientific reason behind the birth of a boy or a girl. In fact the mother is not responsible for the sex of the child and it has been genetically proved that the sex of a newborn is determined by what the child inherits from the father.
rows.solution:
1. In some reptiles, the temperature at which the fertilised eggs are kept determines whether the animals developing in the eggs will be male or female.

2. In snails, individuals can change sex during their lifetime, so their sex is not determined genetically.

rows.subtopic: Lens Formula and Power of a Lens
rows.stem: What is the nature (convergent / divergent) of the combination of a convex lens of power \(+4\) D and a concave lens of power \(-2\) D ?
rows.context:
Many optical instruments consist of a number of lenses. They are combined to increase the magnification and sharpness of the image. The net power (P) of the lenses placed in contact is given by the algebraic sum of the powers of the individual lenses \(\mathrm{P_1, P_2, P_3 \ldots}\) as

\(\mathrm{P = P_1 + P_2 + P_3 \ldots}\)

This is also termed as the simple additive property of the power of lens, widely used to design lens systems of cameras, microscopes and telescopes. These lens systems can have a combination of convex lenses and also concave lenses.
rows.solution: The net power of the combination is \(P = +4 + (-2) = +2\) D. The power is positive, so the combination is convergent.

rows.subtopic: Lens Formula and Power of a Lens
rows.stem: Calculate the focal length of a lens of power \(-2{\cdot}5\) D.
rows.context:
Many optical instruments consist of a number of lenses. They are combined to increase the magnification and sharpness of the image. The net power (P) of the lenses placed in contact is given by the algebraic sum of the powers of the individual lenses \(\mathrm{P_1, P_2, P_3 \ldots}\) as

\(\mathrm{P = P_1 + P_2 + P_3 \ldots}\)

This is also termed as the simple additive property of the power of lens, widely used to design lens systems of cameras, microscopes and telescopes. These lens systems can have a combination of convex lenses and also concave lenses.
rows.solution:
\(f = \dfrac{1}{P} = \dfrac{1}{-2{\cdot}5} = -0{\cdot}4\) m \(= -40\) cm.

The negative sign shows it is a concave (diverging) lens.

rows.stem: Draw a ray diagram to show the nature and position of an image formed by a convex lens of power \(+0{\cdot}1\) D, when an object is placed at a distance of 20 cm from its optical centre.
rows.context:
Many optical instruments consist of a number of lenses. They are combined to increase the magnification and sharpness of the image. The net power (P) of the lenses placed in contact is given by the algebraic sum of the powers of the individual lenses \(\mathrm{P_1, P_2, P_3 \ldots}\) as

\(\mathrm{P = P_1 + P_2 + P_3 \ldots}\)

This is also termed as the simple additive property of the power of lens, widely used to design lens systems of cameras, microscopes and telescopes. These lens systems can have a combination of convex lenses and also concave lenses.
rows.solution:
The focal length is \(f = \dfrac{1}{P} = \dfrac{1}{+0{\cdot}1} = 10\) m \(= 1000\) cm. An object at 20 cm is therefore between the optical centre and the focus, and the convex lens forms a virtual, erect and magnified image on the same side as the object.

Ray diagram: draw the object AB between the optical centre O and the focus \(\mathrm{F_1}\). A ray from A parallel to the principal axis passes, after refraction, through the focus \(\mathrm{F_2}\) on the other side; a ray from A through O goes straight on. The refracted rays diverge; produced backwards (dotted), they meet at A' on the same side as the object, farther from the lens. The image A'B' is virtual, erect and magnified. Draw arrows on the rays to show their direction.

By the lens formula, \(\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{1000} - \dfrac{1}{20} = -\dfrac{49}{1000}\), so \(v \approx -20{\cdot}4\) cm and \(m = \dfrac{v}{u} \approx 1{\cdot}02\). With such a long focal length the image lies just behind the object and is only slightly larger; the diagram shows its nature and position, not its true size.

rows.stem: How is a virtual image formed by a convex lens different from that formed by a concave lens ? Under what conditions do a convex and a concave lens form virtual images ?
rows.context:
Many optical instruments consist of a number of lenses. They are combined to increase the magnification and sharpness of the image. The net power (P) of the lenses placed in contact is given by the algebraic sum of the powers of the individual lenses \(\mathrm{P_1, P_2, P_3 \ldots}\) as

\(\mathrm{P = P_1 + P_2 + P_3 \ldots}\)

This is also termed as the simple additive property of the power of lens, widely used to design lens systems of cameras, microscopes and telescopes. These lens systems can have a combination of convex lenses and also concave lenses.
rows.solution:
The virtual image formed by a convex lens is magnified, while that formed by a concave lens is diminished. (Both are erect and on the same side as the object.)

A convex lens forms a virtual image when the object is between the optical centre and the focus. A concave lens forms a virtual image for every position of the object, anywhere between the optical centre and infinity.
